lessons.title: Kotlin as Android's Preferred Language
lessons.content: Google made Kotlin the preferred Android language in 2019, and most modern Jetpack libraries are Kotlin-first. Real scenario: your app's Compose, Hilt, Room, Flow-based architecture reflects this stack.

lessons.title: Android KTX
lessons.content: KTX extension functions make Android's Java-based framework APIs more idiomatic. Real scenario: sharedPreferences.edit { putString(...) } instead of manual edit()/apply() calls.

lessons.title: ViewModel
lessons.content: Survives configuration changes by being scoped to the Activity/Fragment lifecycle instead of recreated with the UI. Real scenario: your HomeViewModel/LessonListViewModel pattern exposing StateFlow.

codeSnippets.code:
@HiltViewModel
class HomeViewModel @Inject constructor(private val repository: LessonRepository) : ViewModel()

lessons.title: LiveData
lessons.content: An older lifecycle-aware observable data holder, predating StateFlow/Compose. Real scenario: recognizing LiveData in legacy codebases, knowing StateFlow is its modern successor.

codeSnippets.code:
private val _lessons = MutableLiveData<List<Lesson>>()
val lessons: LiveData<List<Lesson>> = _lessons

lessons.title: StateFlow in Android Architecture
lessons.content: The modern standard for exposing UI state, collected via collectAsStateWithLifecycle() to pause when not visible. Real scenario: your HomeScreen composable collecting uiState.

lessons.title: SharedFlow for One-Time Events in Android
lessons.content: The standard way to model one-time UI events since StateFlow's replay would incorrectly re-trigger them. Real scenario: a navigation event emitted through SharedFlow, collected once.

lessons.title: Room Database
lessons.content: Jetpack's SQLite abstraction, generating DAO/database code from annotated entities, with built-in Flow support. Real scenario: your app's LessonEntity, LessonDao, and AppDatabase.

lessons.title: Retrofit
lessons.content: A popular type-safe HTTP client defining API endpoints as annotated interface methods. Real scenario: recognizing Retrofit's @GET/@POST style in Android-only (non-KMP) codebases.

lessons.title: WorkManager
lessons.content: Schedules deferrable, guaranteed background work that runs even if the app is closed. Real scenario: scheduling your app's content sync to run periodically in the background.

lessons.title: Navigation Component / Compose Navigation
lessons.content: Manages a back stack of composable destinations with type-safe navigation. Real scenario: your app's AppNavGraph wiring Home -> LessonList -> LessonDetail.

lessons.title: Compose State Fundamentals
lessons.content: State<T> is observable - reading it inside a Composable subscribes to recomposition on change. Real scenario: your uiState StateFlow becoming Compose State via collectAsState().

codeSnippets.code:
var count by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }
Button(onClick = { count++ }) { Text("Count: $count") }

lessons.title: remember
lessons.content: Caches a value across recompositions within a Composable's lifetime. Real scenario: remembering a filtered list, only recalculated when the source data actually changes.

lessons.title: rememberSaveable
lessons.content: Like remember but survives configuration changes and process death via the instance state Bundle. Real scenario: preserving typed search input across screen rotation.

lessons.title: collectAsState / collectAsStateWithLifecycle
lessons.content: Converts a Flow into Compose State; the lifecycle-aware variant pauses collection when not visible. Real scenario: how HomeScreen observes viewModel.uiState.

lessons.title: Snapshot State System
lessons.content: Compose's State is built on a snapshot system tracking reads/writes to know exactly what to recompose. Real scenario: why mutating a plain var inside a Composable doesn't trigger recomposition.

codeSnippets.code:
var count = 0 // NOT tracked, no recomposition
var tracked by remember { mutableStateOf(0) } // tracked, triggers recomposition
